title: Quantum Kernel k-Means for Credit-Card Fraud Detection:A Controlled Benchmark on Real Transaction Data
summary: We benchmarked quantum kernel $k$-means against classical clustering for credit-card fraud detection on real transaction data, at up to \MaxQubits{} qubits, under a protocol with separated selection and reporting data and matched search budgets. We find no robust quantum advantage: the sign of the difference depends on register size, all effect sizes are below $0.013$ ARI, and the single significant advantage we observe is fully explained by the number of configurations searched.
